## Result

Three files changed:

**proto-blue/Cargo.toml:31**
  `rust-version = "1.85"` -> `rust-version = "1.88"`

**.github/workflows/ci.yml** (new `msrv` job inserted before `docs`)
  Uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.88` + `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`. Comment in the job points future readers at the two files that must be edited together for any MSRV bump.

**README.md:17, 329**
  Both MSRV mentions bumped to 1.88. Added a paragraph at the MSRV section noting let-chains are the binding constraint and that CI verifies it.

## Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting)

  cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked (host 1.95)                PASS (12.19s)
  cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace --all-targets --locked                    PASS (23.09s)
  cargo +1.85 check ...                                                     REFUSED by cargo resolver (correctly)
    -> "proto-blue-* requires rustc 1.88" surfaces from metadata enforcement
    -> bonus finding: icu_* deps (icu_collections, icu_normalizer, icu_properties, icu_provider) require 1.86 anyway, so the v0.3.1 "1.85" declaration was doubly broken
  Verified the new ci.yml `msrv` job step shape matches existing dtolnay/rust-toolchain usage in the file.

## Notes for the human

1. Release decision: this is a packaging fix (the published v0.3.1 manifest lies about MSRV) so a patch v0.3.2 is defensible — no source behavior changes. Alternatively roll it into the next minor.
2. The MSRV CI job is the load-bearing piece. Without it, the next contributor adds an `async fn` trait or another nightly-recent feature and we're back here.
3. CHANGELOG.md auto-update will trigger when this issue closes via the crosslink harness (--no-changelog NOT used on this one — the title is changelog-shaped).
4. Other crates (proto-blue-common, proto-blue-crypto, proto-blue-syntax, etc.) ALSO surfaced as "requires 1.88" in the 1.85 resolver error. That's because workspace inheritance now stamps all of them, not because they have their own let-chains. The original Explore confirmed the user's named three crates were the source.

Category: A (root-cause). The "fix" is to make the declared MSRV match the truth and add a guard so it stays matched. Rewriting 7 let-chains to nested if-lets to keep "1.85" was the alternative (deferred per user choice on the ask-question prompt).
